subject: ULP dev.0.19 / op 1.21.0 — us_to_ticks to 32-bit arithmetic (+48 B), verified bit-exact
body:
A type-width audit of the ULP found exactly ONE libgcc helper in the linked image:
__ashldi3 (40 B), pulled in by udiv64's `den << shift` where shift is a RUNTIME value —
not an RV32 instruction. udiv64 inlines into four hot functions (us_to_ticks, seg_pass,
seg_stalled, bp_enter_dosing), each paying two helper calls per iteration across 45
iterations.

us_to_ticks is now a shift-subtract over the 64-bit numerator held as two 32-bit words,
using 32-bit operations only. `us` is uint32 (4295 s of range; the largest constant in
the file is PARK_SAFETY_TIMEOUT_US = 30 s), the quotient fits uint32 (2^32 us / 7.35
us-per-tick = 5.8e8), and `period` is ~3.86e6 < 2^22 so `rem << 1` cannot overflow.

VERIFIED before writing the code, not after: the exact algorithm was modelled and
compared against the 64-bit reference over the full uint32 `us` domain — edge cases plus
4000 random values, x 6 period values — 0 mismatches in 24084 cases.

CORRECTION TO THE AUDIT that motivated this: it recommended also replacing
`x1000 / PULSES_PER_REV` with the exact identity `x125 / 648` to retire udiv64 and
__ashldi3 entirely, rating it SAFE with a "peak numerator 1.2e9". Independent checking
shows that peak assumes pulse_count = 16. The DOSE BUDGET site multiplies by
bp_dose_target instead (3067 for COLLECT), giving 2.3e11 at the config-max 600 s/rev —
a uint32 overflow. The identity itself IS exact (1000/5184 == 125/648, verified over a
full grid); the range claim is not. Retiring udiv64 needs a bounded or clamped dose
budget first, and belongs in its own image.

Also not taken here: converting the whole tick domain to uint32 (a further -386 B .text
/ -76 B .bss). uint32 ticks wrap at 8.77 h, and 50 sites compare absolute values
(`rtc_ticks() >= deadline`) which is NOT wrap-safe; all 50 must move to the difference
form `(int32_t)(now - dl) >= 0` atomically. A partial conversion is silently wrong and
smaller than the correct one, which is exactly the trap to avoid.

above the warn threshold, not merely above the fail line).

subject: ULP dev.0.18 / op 1.20.0 — fix the three DO-NOT-DEPLOY defects from the adversarial review
body:
The adversarial review of dev.0.17 returned DO NOT DEPLOY. All three defects are fixed
here, plus two budget recoveries.

BLOCKER, now REVERTED — dev.0.17 cancelled BP_PARK_CAL on `test_request == TEST_NONE`.
TEST_NONE (0) is the RESTING value of test_request, not a cancel signal. Consequences,
both confirmed from the tooling: on TestOp, board_script sets bp_park_calibrating and
never touches test_request, so the cancel fired on the first pass and the motor never
turned — calibration broken outright. On operational the same branch never cleared
bp_park_calibrating, which the BP_IDLE dispatcher re-enters on, so
BP_IDLE -> BP_PARK_CAL -> cancel -> BP_IDLE looped at the 1 ms wake period with a
bit-banged DAC write and a wakeup_main_cpu() every iteration — past the 30 s backstop
(the cancel is tested first and the deadline is re-armed each entry) and clearable only
by a power cycle. That is the #46 lightsleep kill path at maximum rate, permanently, and
it was reachable by exactly the host-timeout scenario the change was written for. The
stale-test_request concern is real but needs a token that is not the idle value.

bp_start_signaled is now cleared at EVERY episode entry (6 sites). dev.0.17 introduced it
but cleared it only on a successful kick, so the FIRST BP start-failure was reported and
every subsequent one was silent — and since the CPU read-and-clears motor_stop_events, a
suppressed re-set is lost, not delayed. On a jammed pump the operator would have seen
bare timeouts with no start-FAIL evidence, on the device where that bit is the primary
jam diagnostic.

The dose and park stall branches now LATCH bp_recovery_signaled. Moving the kick onto its
own flag removed the incidental gating those branches relied on, so every stalled pass
emitted MOTOR_STOP_BP + wakeup_main_cpu() at ~3.6/s — the exact wake storm the commit
claimed to fix, made worse by the 3x longer dose backstop.

The past-deadline dose sleep now yields to a running AC. Placed ahead of the AC_RUNNING
check it dropped an actively regulating AC from continuous polling to one seg_pass per
1 ms wake, Nyquist-marginal against its ~1.93 ms transition period; undercounted
intervals read as "too slow" and drive AC power UP — the same undercount family as the
calibration bug.

Kick ordering is now encoder ON -> DAC write -> motor ON. Keeping DAC-before-enable
(so a reload cannot drive at the pre-reset power) while powering the encoder first means
the ~1 ms DAC write doubles as encoder settling, instead of latching kick_level inside
the turn-on transient against an ENCODER_SKIP_PULSES budget of exactly 1.

BUDGET (+92 B): the #56 park stop-verify is DELETED, not repaired — it disabled the
encoder pad and then busy-spun counting edges on it, and init_input leaves both pulls
off, so it read a float: bp_parked was granted by a check that never ran and its
MOTOR_STOP_BP could never fire. Measuring before de-energising does not work either
(DOSE_COAST_US is 1 s and coast-down edges are expected). bp_parked reverts to the
operational criterion that shipped through the 40-hour run. Also removes a 50 ms
BLOCKING busy-spin from the "nothing blocks" fold. seg_stalled now caches its window
instead of recomputing calc_batch_timeout_us + us_to_ticks (64-bit maths) every pass.

Also removed two comments referencing HALT_REASSERT_US, a macro that does not exist
because that feature was removed, and corrected the seg_pass comment that promised a
1 Hz DAC re-assert the code does not implement.

ULP dev.0.17 / op 1.19.0 — six audit fixes; the seventh does not fit in RTC memory
body:
Six CONFIRMED findings from the 3-pass behavioural audit and runs 2026-07-26-002/003:

1. DOSE_DEADLINE_MULT 10 -> 30. The ULP's dose backstop was ~22.2 s on the 50 deg
   PREPARE while the firmware waits 66.7 s, so for 44 s the pump was commanded to
   dose, the ULP had stopped kicking (main.c gates the whole kick+drive block on the
   deadline) and emitted no further MOTOR_START_FAIL_BP. That is the mechanism behind
   the 67-second dead window in the aborted run. 30x matches the firmware exactly.
2. The kick writes the DAC BEFORE energising the motor. Raising enable first left a
   ~1 ms window driving at whatever the DAC7574 still latched — after a CPU reload
   that is the PRE-RESET power.
3. A dose past its deadline now SLEEPS instead of spinning the core at 100 % duty for
   the remainder of the firmware timeout.
4. BP RUNNING stall LATCHES bp_recovery_signaled (the assignment operational had and
   the fold dropped) and the kick gets its OWN persistent flag. Previously a marginal
   pump emitted MOTOR_STOP_BP + wakeup_main_cpu() ~3.6x/s where op emitted one per
   episode — ungated wakes are the #46 lightsleep path. The flag is file-scope, NOT a
   per-call local: try_kick_pass runs every loop pass, so a local would signal every
   50 ms and make it ~6x worse.
5. Park-cancel uses bp_do_stop() instead of a hand-rolled halt that left has_started,
   recovery_signaled, integral, prev_error and the max/min power sentinels stale.
6. BP_PARK_CAL honours TEST_NONE as a cancel, so a firmware that hits its 60 s timeout
   can actually stop the motor, and a stale test_request cannot re-trigger the
   calibration from BP_IDLE later.

NOT FIXED — the 1 Hz hardware HALT re-assert. Implemented, measured, REMOVED: it does
not fit. With it the image had 348 B headroom against a 340 B worst-case stack (8 B of
real margin) versus a 442 B computed gate. Three variants were tried (per-pump
helper, single loop-top deadline, DAC-write-only) and none got under budget. The
finding it addresses is SUSPECTED, not CONFIRMED, so it lost the budget contest. This
is now an RTC-MEMORY problem: the fold plus these fixes exceeds the 8 KB budget.

subject: Gate: a ULP binary must be PROVABLY paired with its address map
body:
WHY: I cited a "1.15.0 rollback pair" repeatedly today as a zero-cost recovery.
It was not a pair. The binary was genuine 1.15.0; the map saved beside it carried
ULP_VARIANT='testop' — a testop-era map. Deploying the two together gave a board
reading every shared variable at the wrong address: ULP_VERSION decoded 0.19.168,
the overflow flag read 6056, the ULP looked DEAD. Nothing detected it. I found it
by hand, after twice mis-reading a cached module as a deployment failure.

That failure mode is worse than misreporting: the firmware WRITES pump commands
through these addresses, so a mismatched pair can poke arbitrary RTC memory, and
the documented consequence is a clobbered stack canary.

THE CHECK is the same self-validating read that finally exposed it on hardware,
done offline: the map states where ULP_VERSION lives, so read that offset out of
the .bin and decode it. A correct pair yields a sane MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH; a
mismatched one yields garbage. Family is checked against SWR-503 as amended
(MAJOR 1 = operational, 9 = TestOp).

finished the 20x2 schedule unattended: 20/20 samples, 41 doses, FINISH, 25 faults,

body:

recitable, so this enforces at the only moment that reliably matters):

   positives (nm cannot tell "#ifdef-ed out" from "static and inlined" — it flagged

   so it now resolves guards in source.
3. testlog.add_finding() REFUSES a finding without verdict (CONFIRMED/SUSPECTED/
   REFUTED), evidence containing a file:line, and a concrete failure_scenario. Four
   mechanisms were asserted on 2026-07-26 from a stale comment, one deduped log line
   and a timing coincidence; each would have failed this gate.

AUDIT — three independent passes (regulate_pump/drive_window/stop_pump; AC service/
sched_idle/entry actions/park cal; plus an adversarial pass told to REFUTE).

My first draft scored 1 of 4. F3, which I flagged CRITICAL, is REFUTED: a 50 ms kick
window holds 16-50 edges and needs 2, at most one AC write can land in it, and
seg_pass compares LEVELS so a 1 ms block cannot hide a 3.09 ms edge. I also called
the transfer "bit-banged" (it is the RTC hardware I2C master) and offered
corroboration that only proved the AC was regulating. F4's defect claim is refuted
and its op comparison was false. F1's conclusion holds but its evidence was wrong
line numbers plus a comment quoted as code.

Tier-1 findings that actually matter, none of which a function-list check could see:
- bp_park_complete measures a DE-ENERGISED, FLOATING encoder: bp_parked is granted
  on a check that never ran, and its MOTOR_STOP_BP can never fire.
- The DAC is never re-asserted; enable_gpio rises ~1 ms before the kick's DAC write,
  so a post-reload kick briefly drives at the pre-reset power.
- TEST_DETERMINE_PARKING is served only from BP_IDLE and TEST_NONE no longer
  cancels: the firmware poll can block forever. The "calibration contract proven
  end-to-end" claim holds only because the firmware idles the BP first.
- RUNNING stall dedupe never latches (`*recovery_signaled = true` dropped) and the
  shared flag is passed into the kick which clears it -> ~3.6 ungated CPU wakes/s
  into the #46 lightsleep path, where op emitted one per episode.
- Stale recovery_signaled can suppress MOTOR_START_FAIL/MOTOR_STOP for a whole
  episode, so "only one escalation logged" cannot distinguish stopped-vs-unreported.
- The turn-on skip is per-ARM not per-WINDOW, so from window 2 a single edge fakes a
  start.
- Post-deadline BP_DOSING spins at 100% duty AND blocks calibration.
- AC service during a BP dose lost its rate limit, 150 ms cap and the 160-edge
  AC_BUSY_DOSE_GUARD that existed to keep I2C off the target crossing.

start_power from the escalated register) — NOT a fold regression, contrary to what I

subject: ULP fold behavioural audit (PARTIAL): 1 regression, 1 defect, 2 of my claims refuted
body:
Audit method: compare the operational function's ACTUAL CODE, statement by
statement, against the fold. Comments in main.c are treated as unverified until
the code confirms them — this audit exists because a stale comment sent me down
a wrong root cause twice in one session.

F1 — try_kick_start step 4b is NOT dropped. My claim was WRONG. The header at
main.c:762 says "stop the motor (DAC->HALT, motor-enable LOW)"; the CODE at
main.c:1651 says "Step 4b (1.9.0): do NOT de-energize", with bench evidence that
a pulsed kick produced ZERO edges from the sealed dead-point while a continuous
drive at power 3000 turned a clean revolution. The fold matches the real op
behaviour. The header is stale documentation — fix the comment, not the code.
Reverting to a pulsed kick would reintroduce the failure 1.9.0 fixed.

F2 — the fold's start bar is MORE permissive than op, not stricter. Op calls
sample_encoder(pulse_target=1) and accepts on count>0; sample_encoder discards 1
turn-on edge, latches t_start on the next, then counts 1 more => op requires
THREE rising edges in 50 ms. Fold dev.0.14/0.15 requires two; dev.0.11-0.13
required one. This REFUTES my "two-edge bar is too strict" hypothesis, and shows
the single-edge accept was the real outlier.

F3 — CRITICAL fold regression: the kick's edge watch is no longer isolated.
Op detects the start inside sample_encoder, a TIGHT BLOCKING busy-poll where
nothing else on the ULP runs, so every transition is seen. The fold samples once
per main-loop pass while the same loop services ac_tick, whose seg_pass does a
bit-banged ~1 ms I2C DAC write on every AC segment close. The BP encoder is
unobserved for that ~1 ms, and at kick speeds an encoder period is shorter than
that, so real edges can be missed - start never confirmed, escalate, repeat,
while the motor may actually be turning. The failing run corroborates: the AC was
regulating during the BP start-FAIL (ac_dac=2429 pwr=1666 spr=20.0).
This is a lost IMPLICIT guarantee (blocking = exclusive encoder access) - exactly
the class a function-list parity check cannot see.

F4 — seg_pass refreshes stall_edge BEFORE the jitter skip, so an edge the code
explicitly classifies as "not a real motion edge" still resets the stall timer.
Op has no equivalent: it decides stall from count==0 returned by sample_encoder,
not a rolling timestamp.

PENDING, explicitly NOT clean: regulate_pump, bp_drive_window, ac_busy_regulate/
ac_busy_hall_service, stop_pump's full side-effect set, test_determine_parking vs
BP_PARK_CAL, the enter_* actions, and sched_idle's sleep gating.

Process finding: the original parity check compared function LISTS and reported
complete parity. It cannot detect a lost timing guarantee (F3) or a reordered
statement (F4), and F1 shows reading even the documented contract is unsafe.

subject: Run 2026-07-26-001 PASS — encoder turn-on skip confirmed as the root cause
body:
10/10 samples to FINISH on TestOp dev.0.15, 20 doses, 0 reboots, 2 faults,
ZERO BP faults.

The decisive number never moved: bp_kick_reg held the baked nominal 895 for the
whole run. On 1.17.0 it ratcheted 1095 -> 495 -> 295 -> 0 (full power) and the
BP visibly over-sped. The only change here was 895 -> 1095, which is power going
DOWN via the existing bp_seed_pid() adoption path — not escalation.

  faults        43 (2.15/sample)  ->  2 (0.20/sample)
  BP faults     43                ->  0
  kick ratchet  1095 -> 0         ->  none
  calibration   failed attempt 1  ->  passed first attempt

Mechanism, evidenced end to end: the encoder is powered down between drives and
during every ladder hold, so its first edge after power-on can be turn-on jitter
rather than rotation. The old sample_encoder discarded ENCODER_SKIP_PULSES such
edges; the fold dropped the guard. A jitter edge then declared the motor started
while the rotor stood still -> no further edges -> seg_stalled -> re-kick ->
ESCALATE, permanently. Restoring the skip means the chain never starts.

This also resolves Sten's "stalls happen exactly at park position, seems
systematic": the drive re-arm after an encoder power-cycle is where a jitter edge
lands, and park is where those power-cycles bunch up. The repeatable rotor angle
was pointing at the ENCODER, not at mechanics.

Both remaining faults are AC-only (BP idle and halted in each). The start-FAIL
may be a side effect of the fix itself — the skip requires TWO rising edges
before declaring a start, and the first edges off rest are far slower than the
3.9 ms/edge of steady state. If AC start-FAILs recur, apply ENCODER_SKIP_PULSES
to the drive re-arm only and leave the kick at one edge.

Also verified: SWR-286 session counter increments once per session start and
persists — 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 across the last five sessions.

Not proven here: TestOp, USB attached, bench. Operational promotion still needs
the op binary re-baselined and a battery/PPK2 run with USB detached.

subject: build_verify_ulp: replace the fixed 768 B stack bar with a per-build computed gate
body:
Sten's observation: the headroom constant was sized for a DEEP call stack, and
the fold doesn't have one any more.

Measured from the linked op image (frame sizes from `add sp,sp,-N` prologues,
call graph from `jal`, longest path):

     20 B  __start
    128 B  main                                   <- the continuous loop
     48 B  bp_drive_pass
     96 B  seg_pass
     32 B  dac7574_write_control
     48 B  ulp_riscv_i2c_master_write_to_device
    ------
    372 B  worst case, 6 frames

So the real requirement is 372 B while the gate demanded 768 B — more than 2x
over-provisioned, and it was blocking images that carry ample margin. The
constant described the PRE-FOLD chain (bp_tick -> regulate_pump ->
sample_encoder -> dac7574 -> i2c, with ac_busy_regulate alongside); dropping
regulate_pump removed the deepest nesting along with 800 B of code.

New gate derives itself per build:
    FAIL  headroom < max(need * 1.3, need + 64)
    WARN  headroom < max(need * 1.5, need + 128)   (reported as "thin")
1.3x covers observed compiler drift (frames move 16-32 B across rebuilds) plus
one unforeseen ~48 B frame; the 4 B canary remains the hard backstop. Because
`need` is recomputed from the image, the gate TIGHTENS ITSELF automatically if
anyone re-nests the call graph — which a fixed constant can never do.

Result:  operational need=372 gate=483 headroom=508 (thin, PASS)
         test        need=260 gate=338 headroom=1884 (ok)
         test2       need=260 gate=338 headroom=3424 (ok)

Sound because the ULP has no recursion (guarded), no indirect calls, no libgcc
helpers (checked separately) and RISC-V has no red zone. It does NOT model an
async frame pushed by the ROM wake path — a stack low-water probe should
confirm it empirically before this is leaned on for an operational release.
Precedent: ULP 1.14.0's trust gate measured 228 B low-water.

I had also been quoting the bar as 512 B in discussion; the code said 768.
Corrected here.

subject: ULP dev.0.15 / op 1.18.0 — withdraw the two power-steering fixes; keep the two conservative ones
body:
dev.0.14 shipped four changes at once. Two of them STEER POWER — re-seed Simple-P
from nominal on every successful kick (handover), and decay the learned kick power
back toward nominal — and they destabilised the AC immediately: on the bench the
pump moved in tiny jerks 2-3 per second during the anticoagulant prime.

That cadence convicts them. At the AC's 20 s/rev the measurement burst is ~70 ms
(16 intervals at 3.9 ms/edge) and the ladder holds 256/512 ms at levels 7-8, so
330-500 ms IS the regulation cycle. The motor was stepping once per CONTROL UPDATE,
not once per revolution — the operating point was being reset every cycle.

Root of the mistake: escalation is load-bearing on this hardware. Nominal power is
marginal (the same fact the park hard spot demonstrates), so the escalated power is
what keeps the pump turning. Punishing every SUCCESSFUL start with a decay turns it
into an oscillator: start nominal -> too weak -> stall -> kick escalates -> decay
pulls it back down -> stall. 1.17.0 ratcheted one way and over-sped; dev.0.14
oscillated. Both are the same underlying fact seen from opposite sides.

KEPT (conservative — they only suppress FALSE signals, they cannot steer power):
  (1) encoder turn-on skip in both the kick and the drive re-arm;
  (4) BP_PARK_OFFSET stall detection.
The turn-on skip is exonerated by the same timing that convicts the others: it
discards 1 edge in ~17 at 3.9 ms/edge, far too small to produce a visible step.

PROCESS: stacking four changes in one image broke my own standing rule (one change
per image, boot-prove each) — the rule I have written down for MCU config and did
not apply to ULP control changes. The pump reported it within one prime.

Op headroom 420 -> 508 B (the dead handover GC'd out); still 4 B under the 512 B
bar, so op promotion stays blocked. TestOp (~1.8 KB spare) is unaffected.

subject: ULP 1.18.0 — four fixes for the run 2026-07-25-001 stall/over-speed chain (NOT deployable yet: op headroom 420 < 512)
body:
Owner direction: keep Simple-P with frequent regulation on park + dose (no
ladder there), and do NOT add a power floor — the ladder and Simple-P are what
hold speed.

(1) ENCODER TURN-ON SKIP RESTORED — the driver of everything else.
    The encoder is powered down during a ladder hold and between drives; its
    first edge after power-on can be turn-on jitter, not rotation. The old
    sample_encoder discarded ENCODER_SKIP_PULSES such edges, and Test2 1.4.1
    raised its start bar for exactly this ("a single encoder turn-on-jitter edge
    FAKED STARTS — 'Started 2 ms, run edges 0'"). The fold dropped the guard, so
    a jitter edge declared the motor started while the rotor stood still -> no
    further edges -> seg_stalled -> re-kick -> ESCALATE. Now discarded in BOTH
    the kick (try_kick_pass) and the drive re-arm (seg_reset/seg_pass), so a
    jitter edge can neither fake a start nor corrupt the interval timing.
(2) SANE HANDOVER — a successful kick re-arms first_update so Simple-P re-seeds
    from the nominal start power instead of inheriting the escalated kick power
    the motor was started at.
(3) DECAY — a successful start relaxes the learned kick one escalate-step back
    toward the baked nominal. Escalation previously only ever rose, and
    bp_seed_pid() derives start_power FROM it, so one hard spot permanently
    over-powered every later drive: measured 1095 -> 495 -> 295 -> 0 (FULL
    power) across a single 20-sample session.
(4) BP_PARK_OFFSET STALL DETECTION — the centre-coast into the sealed park
    position had none, so a rotor stalled exactly there (where the owner
    observes the stalls) was never reported and the motor was held energised
    against it for the full 5 s backstop. Detected via the existing deadline.

WHY THIS SLIPPED PAST VERIFICATION: test_ulp_source.py asserts on
sample_encoder, which still exists in main.c under #ifndef ULP_FOLD_BUILD and
is compiled OUT of the shipping binary. The tests kept passing against the
rolled-back path while the code that ships was never checked — exactly the
category-B gap already written up in docs/ulp_1.17.0_verification_status.md,
where SWR-126 (the kick / sample_encoder requirement) is listed. My op-parity
review also compared function LISTS, not the guards inside each function.

NOT DEPLOYED. Operational headroom 596 -> 420 B, below the 512 B FAIL bar
(the #48/#36 stack-overflow class). Reclaimed 340 -> 380 -> 420 by merging the
two turn-on counters into one seg_t field, detecting the park-offset stall from
the existing deadline instead of new stall machinery, and decaying toward
compile-time nominals instead of runtime-captured ones. Still short.

scheduler design §2.1a: PROBE RESULT — ULP cannot read PCNT (hybrid decided)
body:
Built a TESTOP peripheral-read probe (TEST_PEEK loads *(uint32_t*)peek_addr
from the ULP; probe-only mode, no canary confound) and ran it live. The ULP
reads RTC-domain registers exactly (both control magics) but every HP/APB read
fails — PCNT reads returned the ADDRESS ITSELF (0x600170FC for addr
0x600170FC), the signature of a load that never reaches the bus. Proven: the
S3 ULP RISC-V cannot access HP peripherals; PCNT is unreachable from the ULP.

=> the fully non-blocking counter-compare endpoint is NOT feasible; the
redesign is bounded to the HYBRID (bounded bit-bang poll windows + fair
dispatch). All correctness wins (#48/#55/#56) survive. Reusable probe saved to
tools/ulp_probe/. ULP source reverted clean (probe was TESTOP-only, one-shot).

subject: design note §2.1: hardware-counter spike — it's CPU-side, not ULP-side
body:
Git archaeology of Mirza's counter work: PCNT was implemented May-Jun
2025 as CPU-side esp32.PCNT (custom mpy build) during CPU-regulation
era; NO ULP commit has ever used a hardware counter; the ULP RISC-V
regulator (1aa9d2c, 2026-04-02) has always bit-banged (5184 steps/rev,
gpio_get_level). 'Hardware counters available to the ULP' is a
conflation. Corrected the note's false premise; the live open question
is now whether the S3 ULP can read PCNT at all (TRM + bench probe),
which decides pure-loop vs hybrid. Correctness fixes need no counter.

subject: design note: ULP cooperative non-blocking scheduler (branch start)
body:
Captures the architecture Sten proposed — single flat non-blocking main
loop, hardware edge counters (Mirza-validated), MoveTo/SimpleP/hall-flag
dispatch — as the structural cure for #48/#55/#56 (the multi-second
dose/coast/park blocking windows are the shared root).

Includes the adversarial check on 'never sleep': the correctness win is
NON-BLOCKING (orthogonal to sleeping); continuous spin helps only
stop-precision latency during active motion and wastes battery during
idle — so 'don't sleep while working, sleep while idle', state-driven.
Plus loop-rate analysis (counting decoupled from rate by HW counters;
rate set by stop precision), #53 caution (no ULP-side clock defense),
RTC-bus-contention + DAC-write-on-change, and a staged TestOp migration.

subject: ULP 1.12.0: cooperative AC service through BP dose/coast/park busy loops (SWR-271)
body:
Root cause of the 8h run's residual ~3/h false AC hall warnings: BP_DOSING /
BP_DOSE_COAST / BP_PARKING hold the ULP inside blocking loops for the whole
dose (~10 s), coast (5 s) and park (<=30 s) — ac_tick() never runs there, so
an AC hall pass falling inside such a window was LOST outright (a lost pass
reads as a 2x-SPR counter gap on the CPU monitor => false 'did not advance'
warning) and the AC ran open-loop on its held DAC — the owner's masking
diagnosis, confirmed in source and fixed per his 'task scheduler in the ULP
Dose/Park' direction.

ac_busy_hall_service(): ac_tick's exact hall block (level mirror, 1->0 count,
CPU wake), now shared by ac_tick and called inside every blocking BP spin
(bp_drive_window, coast, park centre-offset) — no AC revolution can be lost
to a BP busy window. ac_busy_regulate(): every-16th-window (~0.8 s), 150 ms-
capped, 8-interval AC Simple-P slice between BP drive windows in DOSING and
PARKING; its combined poll keeps counting BP encoder edges into the caller's
ledger so dose/park tick accounting stays EXACT; dose-tail guard (160 edges)
keeps target-crossing out of any slice; the park slice watches the BP hall so
home is never overshot; no kick/ladder/stall-recovery coupling. ac_busy_slices
telemetry proves regulation ran.

Gates: canary linked, no libgcc, op headroom 696 B (was 1296; LOW accepted —
max call depth unchanged vs the existing regulate_pump->run_simple_p chain,
.stack_canary + firmware per-tick check armed, 184 B above the 512 fail
line). Registry 1.64: SWR-271 + 5 structure tests; 138 reqs, 120 PASS, 0
FAIL. Deploy pending board-on-USB.
